title: Static hosting and deployment concepts
learningObjectives: Explain static hosting and deployment concepts and apply it to accessible, reliable web development.

understand.concept: Static hosting serves files such as HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, and JSON without requiring a server-side application for each request. Deployment publishes a tested build to a hosting environment. A CDN may distribute static assets closer to users.
understand.whyItMatters: Static hosting can be simple and scalable, but client-side code cannot securely hold secrets or enforce privileged business rules. Deployment also needs cache strategy, HTTPS, and rollback planning.
understand.analogy: Static hosting is like publishing a prepared set of pages for visitors to retrieve directly.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; web protocols, browser behaviour, and accessibility requirements follow formal standards and platform implementations.

explain.narrative: The example lists typical static assets. A real hosting provider serves them through its configured origin and CDN.

examples.explanation: The example lists typical static assets. A real hosting provider serves them through its configured origin and CDN.
examples.expectedOutput: The example illustrates the concept; some browser examples require a real served page and supported APIs.

practise.guidedTask: Prepare a deployment checklist for a static learning site: build output, routing, HTTPS, cache headers, environment configuration, and rollback.
practise.independentTask: Apply the concept to a small web page. Record the expected behaviour, how you tested it, and any limitations or fallbacks.
hints: Use browser developer tools to inspect actual behaviour.
Test with keyboard and different viewport sizes.
Keep core content available when enhancements are unsupported.
